answer: In this design, each identity must complete a verifiable delay function by performing a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every step depends on the prior result. GPUs may evaluate separate identities concurrently, but cannot shortcut one chain through parallel work; each clone therefore incurs its own sequential wall-clock delay. The ember, willow, and inlet labels do not change this cost: creating many Sybil identities demands proportionally more computation or time, giving verification a physical bottleneck rather than relying on names alone.
